sentences: In 1981, a man is a party clown and aspiring stand-up comedian who lives with his mother in a crime-ridden city.
He suffers from a neurological disorder that causes him to have random, uncontrollable laughing fits, for which he takes medication that he obtains through the city's social services program.
After the man is attacked by street youths while on the job, his co-worker gives him a revolver to defend himself.
The man pursues a relationship with his neighbor, a single mother, and invites her to see his routine at a comedy club.
Later, while performing at a children's hospital, the man's gun accidentally falls out of his pocket, resulting in him getting fired.
While riding home on the subway and still wearing his clown make-up, he is mocked and assaulted by three drunk employees from a company.
He fatally shoots two of them in self-defense and murders the third as he attempts to flee.
Their employer, a billionaire mayoral candidate, condemns the killings, but supporters begin sporting clown masks in the man's image.
Budget cuts shut down the social services program, leaving the man without his medication.
The neighbor attends the man's stand-up routine, which fails due to his disorder and his jokes falling flat.
The man intercepts a letter from his mother to the billionaire indicating that he is the billionaire's illegitimate son, and berates his mother for hiding the truth of his parentage.
He goes to the billionaire's manor, where he meets the billionaire's young son, but flees after a scuffle with the family butler.
His mother suffers a stroke after being questioned by two detectives investigating the man's involvement in the subway murders, and is hospitalized.
The man's idol, a popular late-night talk show host, presents clips of the man's failed performance on his show and mockingly calls him a "joker", much to the man's distress.
The man confronts the billionaire at a movie theater.
The billionaire denies being his father, claiming that his mother also is not his biological mother.
The man visits the state hospital and reads his mother's file, which states she was a delusional narcissist who adopted the man while working as a housekeeper for the billionaire's family.
She developed an imaginary intimate relationship with the billionaire, which included the man being their biological son.
At the same time, his mother raised the man with a boyfriend who physically and sexually abused them, leading to his neurological disorder.
The distraught man enters the neighbor's apartment unannounced.
Frightened, she kindly asks him to leave, revealing their relationship to be a figment of the man's imagination.
The following day, the man smothers his mother with a pillow at the hospital.
The man is invited onto the host's show and prepares by crafting a clown-themed persona.
He is visited by his co-worker and another ex-colleague.
The man fatally stabs and beats the co-worker, but spares the other ex-colleague for being kind to him in the past.
The detectives investigating the man pursue him onto a train filled with clown protesters.
The man incites a brawl, during which one detective accidentally shoots and kills a protester.
The other protesters, in turn, beat the detectives while the man escapes.
At the studio, the man asks the host to introduce him by a new name, a reference to his earlier mockery.
As the show broadcasts live, the man tells morbid jokes, confesses to the subway murders, rants about societal neglect of the downtrodden, and berates the host for ridiculing him.
After a final joke, the man shoots the host in the head, killing him.
The man is arrested, and riots erupt across the city.
Looters in an ambulance crash into the police car carrying the man and free him.
Meanwhile, one rioter corners the billionaire's family in an alley and murders the billionaire and his wife in front of their son.
The man stands atop the police car, dances to the cheers of the crowd, and smears the blood on his face into a smile.
Sometime later at the state hospital, the man laughs to himself about a joke during a session with his new therapist.
He declines telling it to her, claiming she would not understand it.
He leaves behind a trail of bloodied shoeprints as an orderly chases him down.
On Halloween, the city's mayor is murdered by a masked serial killer.

A reclusive billionaire, who has operated for two years as a vigilante, investigates the murder alongside a police lieutenant, much to the disdain of the city's police department; the killer leaves a message for the vigilante at the crime scene.
The following night, the killer kills the police commissioner and leaves another message for the vigilante.

The vigilante and the lieutenant discover that the killer left a thumb drive in the mayor's car; it contains images of the mayor's affair with a woman at a nightclub operated by a gangster, the crime boss's lieutenant.
While questioning the gangster, who pleads ignorance, the vigilante notices that the woman's roommate works at the club as a waitress.
The woman disappears; while searching for answers, the vigilante and the waitress discover that the commissioner and the mayor were on the crime boss's payroll, as is the district attorney.
The killer abducts the district attorney, straps a timed collar bomb to his neck, and sends him to interrupt the mayor's funeral.
When the vigilante arrives, the killer calls him via a phone duct-taped to the district attorney and threatens to detonate the bomb if the district attorney cannot answer three riddles.
The district attorney refuses to answer the third—the name of the informant who gave the police information that led to a historic drug bust ending a mob boss's operation—and is killed.
The vigilante and the lieutenant deduce that the informant may be the gangster and track him to a drug deal.
They discover that the mob boss's operation was transferred to the crime boss, with many corrupt officers involved.
The waitress inadvertently exposes them when she arrives to steal money and discovers the woman's corpse in the trunk of a car.
The vigilante captures the gangster after a car chase, but he and the lieutenant learn that the gangster is not the informant.

The vigilante and the lieutenant follow the killer's trail to the ruins of an orphanage initially funded by the billionaire's deceased parents, where they learn that the killer holds a grudge against the billionaire's family for failing the orphanage.
The billionaire's butler and caretaker is hospitalized after opening a letter bomb addressed to the billionaire.

The killer leaks evidence that the billionaire's father, who was running for mayor before he was murdered, hired the crime boss to kill a journalist whom the mob boss controlled and was writing a story about the billionaire's mother's family history of mental illness.

The billionaire confronts the butler, who maintains that the billionaire's father only asked the crime boss to threaten the journalist into silence; upon learning that the crime boss had murdered the journalist, the father planned to turn both himself and the crime boss over to the police.
The butler has suspicions that the crime boss had the billionaire's parents killed to silence them, but has no proof of it, stating that the murder could have been perpetrated by any random criminal.
The waitress reveals to the vigilante that the crime boss is her father.
After discovering that the crime boss killed the woman because she learned he was the informant, the waitress attempts to kill him, but the vigilante and the lieutenant arrive in time to stop her.
The lieutenant arrests the crime boss, but the killer kills the crime boss with a sniper rifle moments later.
The killer gives himself up and is unmasked as a forensic accountant; he is incarcerated in the state hospital, where he tells the vigilante he took inspiration from him when targeting the corrupt.
The vigilante learns that the killer has planted car bombs and cultivated an online following that plans to assassinate the mayor-elect.
The bombs destroy the seawall around the city and flood the city.
The killer's followers attempt to kill the mayor-elect at her victory celebration in an arena, but the vigilante and the waitress stop them.
The vigilante saves the crowds in the flooding arena from electrocution and leads them to safety.
In the aftermath, the distraught killer is comforted by another inmate, while the waitress deems the city beyond saving and leaves.
The vigilante continues to aid the city's recovery efforts and vows to inspire hope in the city rather than exacting vengeance.
The story begins with a poor miller who, upon his death, leaves his possessions to his three sons.
The eldest inherits the mill, the second son gets a donkey, and the youngest son is left with only a cat.

The youngest son laments his poor inheritance, but the cat, who turns out to be extraordinarily clever and resourceful, assures his master that he can bring him great fortune if provided with a pair of boots and a simple sack.
Once outfitted with boots, the cat sets out to catch game, such as rabbits and partridges, by using cunning traps.
He presents these animals as gifts to the king, claiming they are from his master, who he names a "marquis".
Over time, the cat builds a reputation for his master as a wealthy and generous nobleman, even though his master is actually a poor miller’s son.
One day, knowing the king and his daughter will be riding by the river, the cat instructs his master to bathe in the water.
As the king's carriage approaches, the cat pretends that his master has been robbed of his fine clothes and is drowning.
The king stops to help and, believing the cat’s story, offers his own fine garments to the miller’s son.
Impressed by the supposed marquis's appearance and the many gifts he had previously received, the king invites him into his carriage.
The princess becomes enamored with the young man.
While traveling, the cat races ahead to a grand castle owned by a powerful and fearsome ogre who has magical powers, including the ability to shapeshift.
The cat flatters the ogre and tricks him into transforming into a small mouse, which the cat immediately devours.
With the ogre gone, the cat claims the castle and its lands for his master.
When the king arrives at the castle and sees its magnificence, he is further convinced of the marquis's wealth and status.
Delighted, he offers his daughter's hand in marriage to the miller's son.

The marriage is celebrated with a grand feast, and the miller's son, now truly a "marquis", lives happily ever after with the princess, thanks to the cleverness and loyalty of the cat, who himself becomes a lord and never has to hunt mice again—unless he wants to for fun.

Shortly before the leader's escape from his exile on an island in 1815, a sailor, the young first mate of a merchant ship, honours his dying captain's last wish: to retrieve a letter from the island, to be conveyed to a supporter of the leader in the city.
When the ship arrives in the port, the ship's owner decides to promote the sailor to captain, provoking the distaste and jealousy of the supercargo.
The shipowner, a sympathizer of the leader himself, provides the sailor with two weeks' furlough to marry his Catalan fiancée and deliver the letter.
The fiancée's cousin is jealous of the sailor, desiring to marry the fiancée himself.
He and the supercargo meet to plan the sailor's downfall: they draft an anonymous letter denouncing the sailor as a supporter of the leader.
The sailor's neighbour, who also resents the sailor's success, objects to the plan, but is unable to prevent them from sending the letter to the crown prosecutor.
The sailor's and the fiancée's engagement party is interrupted by the sailor's arrest; the cowardly neighbour, despite knowing the charges are false, does not speak up.
The sailor is brought before the deputy crown prosecutor.
The prosecutor is the supporter's son, and knows that his political career would be ruined if it were known that his father is a supporter of the leader.
Therefore he destroys the letter and, despite believing the sailor to be innocent, silences him by sentencing him without trial to life imprisonment in the notorious prison.
After six years of imprisonment the sailor is on the verge of suicide.
However, another prisoner, a scholarly Italian priest, digs an escape tunnel that mistakenly ends in the sailor's cell.
The priest helps the sailor deduce the culprits of his imprisonment.
Over the next eight years, the priest educates the sailor in languages, history, culture, mathematics, medicine, and science.
Knowing himself to be close to death from catalepsy, the priest tells the sailor the location of a vast treasure hidden by his former employer on an island.
When the priest dies, the sailor takes the priest's place in the burial sack, which the guards throw into the sea.
The sailor cuts through the sack and swims to a nearby island, where, claiming to be a shipwrecked sailor, he is rescued by Genoese smugglers.
Months later, he locates and retrieves the treasure; he later purchases the island and the title of count from the Tuscan government.
Having sworn vengeance on the supercargo, the cousin, and the prosecutor, the sailor returns to the port in search of information to accomplish his goal.
Travelling as a priest, the sailor finds the neighbour, who regrets not intervening in the sailor's arrest.
The neighbour informs him that the fiancée eventually resigned herself to marrying the cousin.

He recounts that the sailor's father died of starvation, and that the shipowner tried unsuccessfully to secure the sailor's release and save his father, but now the shipowner is on the brink of bankruptcy.
Both the supercargo and the cousin have prospered greatly.
The supercargo became a speculator, amassed a fortune, married a wealthy widow, and became a baron.
The cousin served in the army, rising to the rank of lieutenant-colonel.
The sailor rewards the neighbour with a diamond, but he does not disclose his real identity.
Later, the neighbour negotiates the sale of the diamond to a jeweller, but he kills the jeweller to keep the diamond and the money.
He is eventually arrested and sentenced to the galleys.
To rescue the shipowner from bankruptcy, the sailor poses as a banker, buys the shipowner's debts, and gives him three months' reprieve.

At the end of the three months, the shipowner is about to commit suicide, but learns that the debts have been mysteriously paid and that one of his lost ships has returned with a full cargo; it was secretly rebuilt and laden by the sailor.
The sailor reappears in 1838 as a mysterious, fabulously wealthy count.
The cousin is now a count, the supercargo is a baron and banker, and the prosecutor is a royal prosecutor.
In another city, at Carnival time, the sailor befriends a viscount, the son of the fiancée and the cousin.
He arranges for the viscount to be captured by a bandit (an ally of the sailor), and "rescues" the boy, earning his trust.
The viscount introduces the count to the city's high society.
In his guise as the count, the sailor meets the fiancée for the first time in 23 years and eventually makes the acquaintance of the supercargo, the cousin and the prosecutor.
The count purchases a home in a suburb of the city.

He has learnt from his servant that it is the home in which the prosecutor once had an extramarital affair with the supercargo's wife, who gave birth to a child that the prosecutor buried alive in order to cover up the affair.
The infant was rescued by the servant and raised by the servant's sister, but the child turned to a life of crime as a young man, murdered the sister, and was sentenced to the galleys.
Having impressed the city's society with his wealth and air of mystery, the count sets up the pieces for his revenge.
In 1881, a doctor returns to the city after serving in a war and starts looking for a place to live.
An old friend of his tells him that a detective is looking for someone to split the rent at a flat but cautions the doctor about the detective's eccentricities.
The detective and the doctor meet and, after assessing each other and the rooms, they move in.
The detective is a "consulting detective", and his frequent guests are clients.
After a demonstration of the detective's deductive skills, the doctor's disbelief turns into astonishment.
A telegram requests a consultation in a murder case.
The doctor accompanies the detective to the crime scene, an abandoned house on a road.
Two inspectors are already on the scene.
The victim is a man from another city, and documents found on his person reveal that he has a secretary.
The room is splashed in blood, and the word "RACHE" (German for "revenge") is written in it on one wall; however, the victim's body shows no wounds.
Dismissing the message as a ploy to mislead the police, the detective deduces that the victim was poisoned and supplies a description of the murderer.
Upon moving the victim's body, they discover a woman's gold wedding ring.
The detective places notices in several newspapers about the ring and buys a facsimile of it, hoping to draw the murderer – who has apparently already tried to retrieve the ring – out of hiding.
An old woman answers the advertisement, claiming that the ring belongs to her daughter.
The detective gives her the duplicate and follows her, but she evades him in a way that leads the detective to believe that "she" was actually a young man in disguise, an accomplice to the murderer.
A day later, one of the inspectors visits the detective and the doctor, telling them that he has arrested a suspect.
He went to a landlady's boarding house where the victim and the secretary stayed before the murder.
The victim, a drunk, attempted to kiss the landlady's daughter, which caused their immediate eviction.
He, however, came back later that night and attempted to grab the daughter, prompting her older brother to attack him.
He attempted to chase the victim with a cudgel but claimed to have lost sight of him.
The inspector has him in custody on this circumstantial evidence.
The secretary is later found dead in his hotel room, stabbed through the heart and with the word "RACHE" written in blood on the wall.
The only things the secretary had with him were a novel, a pipe, a telegram saying "he is abroad", and a small box containing two pills.
The detective tests the pills on an old and sickly Scottish Terrier in residence at the flat.
The first pill produces no evident effect, but the second kills the terrier.
A young street urchin then arrives.
He is the leader of a group of street children the detective employs to help him occasionally.
The urchin has summoned a cab the detective wanted.
The detective sends him down to fetch the cabby, claiming to need help with his luggage.
When the cabby comes upstairs, the detective handcuffs and restrains him.
The captive cabby is the murderer of the victim and the secretary.

In a valley in 1847, a man and a little girl, the only survivors of a small party of pioneers, are rescued from death by a party of Latter-day Saints led by their leader, but only on the condition that they adopt and live under the Mormon faith.
Years later in 1860, the now-grown girl befriends and falls in love with the cabby.
However, the leader forbids her from marrying outside the faith and demands that she marry either the secretary or the victim, both sons of members of the church's council.
The man, who has adopted the girl and sworn never to marry his daughter to a Mormon, sends word to the cabby in order to help them escape.
The girl is given one month to choose between her suitors.
The cabby arrives on the eve of the last day, and they all escape under cover of darkness.
While the cabby is hunting in the mountains, the Mormons catch up to the escapees; the secretary kills the man, while the girl is taken back to the Mormons' settlement and forced to marry the victim.
She dies of a broken heart less than a month later.
The cabby breaks into the victim's house the night before the girl's funeral to kiss her body and remove her wedding ring.
A newly qualified English solicitor visits a count at his castle in the mountains to help the count purchase a house near the city.
Ignoring the count's warning, the solicitor wanders the castle at night and encounters three vampire women; the count intervenes and gives the women a bag containing a kidnapped child.
Six weeks later, the count leaves the castle, abandoning the solicitor to the women.
The solicitor, having realised the count's true nature, escapes and ends up delirious in a hospital.
The count takes a ship overseas with boxes of earth from his castle.
The captain's log narrates the crew's disappearance, until only he remains.
When the ship runs aground at a coastal town, a large dog is seen leaping ashore and the captain's corpse is found tied to the helm.
A young woman's letter to her best friend, the solicitor's fiancée, describes her marriage proposals from a doctor, a second suitor, and a third suitor.
The young woman accepts the third suitor's, but all remain friends.
The fiancée joins the young woman on holiday in the coastal town.
The young woman begins to sleepwalk, unaware that the count is influencing her mind.
The fiancée receives a letter about her missing fiancé's illness and goes to the hospital to nurse him.
The young woman becomes very ill; the doctor's old teacher — a professor — determines the nature of her condition, but he refuses to disclose it, instead diagnosing it as acute blood-loss.
The young woman is given fresh blood and placed in a room filled with garlic flowers.
Unaware that vampires cannot tolerate garlic, her mother removes the flowers.
While the doctor and the professor are absent, the young woman and her mother are confronted by a wolf, causing her mother to die of a heart attack.
The young woman dies shortly thereafter.
After her burial, newspapers report children being stalked in the night by a "bloofer lady" (beautiful lady), and the professor deduces it is the young woman.
The doctor, the second suitor, the third suitor, and the professor go to her tomb and see that she is a vampire.
They stake her heart, behead her, and fill her mouth with garlic.
The solicitor and his new bride return and join the campaign against the count.
The group move to the doctor's asylum, and the professor explains that they must destroy the boxes of earth to weaken the count's power.
The count communicates with the doctor's patient, an insane man who eats vermin to absorb their life force.
After the count learns of the group's plot against him, he uses the patient to enter the asylum.
He secretly attacks the solicitor's wife three times, drinking her blood before forcing her to drink his on the final visit, thereby cursing her to become a vampire after death.
The men discover that the count has distributed his boxes of earth around various properties in the city.
After sterilizing most of the boxes, the group fail to trap the count in his city house and learns that the count is fleeing to his castle in the mountains with his last box.
Using hypnosis, the professor exploits the wife's faint psychic connection to the count to track his movements and they pursue, guided by the wife.
In a town, the hunters split up.
The professor and the wife go to the count's castle, where the professor destroys the vampire women.
The solicitor and the third suitor pursue the count's boat on the river, while the second suitor and the doctor follow them on land.
The count's box is loaded onto a wagon by Romani men; the hunters attack and rout the Romani.
The solicitor decapitates the count as the second suitor stabs him in the heart.
The count crumbles to dust, freeing the wife from her vampiric curse.
The second suitor is mortally wounded in the fight against the Romani.
He dies, at peace knowing that the wife is saved.
A note by the solicitor seven years later states that the couple have a son, named after their friend.
In 1792, an early stage of the revolution, a beautiful French actress is married to a wealthy English fop, a baronet.

Before their marriage the actress took revenge upon a marquis, who had ordered her beloved brother beaten for his romantic interest in the marquis' daughter, with the unintended consequence that the marquis and his sons were guillotined.
When the baronet found out, he became estranged from his wife.
The actress, for her part, became disillusioned with the baronet's shallow, dandyish lifestyle.

Meanwhile, the league, a secret society of twenty English aristocrats, "one to command, and nineteen to obey", is engaged in rescuing their French counterparts from the daily executions of the terror.
Their leader, the mysterious rescuer, takes his nom de guerre from the small, red wayside flower he draws on his messages.
Despite being the talk of the city's society, only his followers and possibly the prince know the rescuer's true identity.
Like many others, the actress is entranced by the rescuer's daring exploits.
At a ball attended by the couple, the baronet's verse about the "elusive" rescuer becomes an instant success.
But the actress is being blackmailed by the wily new French envoy to the country: the envoy's agents have stolen a letter proving that her brother is in league with the rescuer.
The envoy offers to trade her brother's life for her help against the rescuer.
Contemptuous of her seemingly witless and unloving husband, the actress does not go to him for help or advice.
Instead, she passes along information which enables the envoy to learn the rescuer's true identity.
Later that night, the actress finally tells her husband of the terrible danger threatening her brother and pleads for his help.
The baronet promises to save him.
After the baronet unexpectedly leaves the country, the actress discovers to her horror (and simultaneous delight) that he is the rescuer.
He had hidden behind the persona of a dull, slow-witted fop to deceive the world.
He had not told the actress because of his worry that she might betray him, as she had the marquis.
Desperate to save her husband, she decides to pursue the baronet abroad to warn him that the envoy knows his identity and his purpose.
She persuades a gentleman to accompany her, but because of the tide and the weather, neither they nor the envoy can leave immediately.
At a port, the baronet openly approaches the envoy in a decrepit inn whose owner is in the baronet's pay.
Despite the envoy's best efforts, the Englishman escapes by offering the envoy a pinch of snuff, which turns out to be pure pepper.
Through a bold plan executed right under the envoy's nose, the baronet rescues the actress's brother and a count, the father of a schoolfriend of the actress's.
The actress pursues the baronet right to the very end, determined to either warn him or share his fate.
The baronet, heavily disguised, is captured by the envoy, who does not recognise him, so he is able to escape.
With the actress's love and courage amply proven, the baronet's ardour is rekindled.
Safely back on board their schooner, the happily reconciled couple returns home.
Soon after, the gentleman marries the count's daughter.
The hero is urgently called home by his father.
To all outward appearances, he is the foppish son of a wealthy ranchero, the former alcalde, having returned home after his military education abroad.
The hero is horrified at the way the common people are mistreated by the corrupt new alcalde.

The hero quickly adopts the guise of a masked outlaw dressed entirely in black, who becomes the defender of the common people and a champion for justice against the uncaring alcalde and his garrison of brutish soldiers.
In the meantime, he romances the alcalde's beautiful and innocent niece, whom he grows to love.
As part of his plan, the hero simultaneously flirts with the alcalde's wife, filling her head with tales of fashion and culture while nurturing her desire to finally get rid of her cruel husband.
In both his guises, the hero must always contend with the governor's most capable henchman, the malevolent and deadly captain.
When the situation comes to a head, he eventually dispatches the captain during a fast-moving saber duel-to-the-death, as the alcalde looks on in astonishment.
This action leads to a forced regime change with the help of the people of the town, the other landowners, and his father, and the alcalde is defeated.
The owner of a set of emeralds receives a letter stating that the emeralds will be stolen at midnight by a criminal, and that police will not be able to stop the robbery.
The criminal, a figure dressed as a bat, murders the owner and steals the emeralds.
The criminal leaves a bat-shaped note for the chief of police to inform him that he will be traveling to the country.
The criminal travels by car to a mansion built by the president of a bank, who has recently been found dead in another state.
The mansion is being rented for the summer by a writer, whose maid sets up a bear trap to catch the criminal.
The bank president's spendthrift nephew wishes to lease the mansion, and plans with a doctor
to frighten the writer away.
The newspaper reports that a cashier at the bank has robbed the bank of $200,000 and has disappeared.
The writer's niece arrives with a supposed new gardener.
The writer asks the gardener about his knowledge on alopecia, urticaria, and rubeola, and he answers as if the terms referred to plants rather than medical conditions.
On the staircase, the nephew is shot, and the niece manages to snatch part of a blueprint of the house from his pocket.
A detective accuses her of trying to find a supposed hidden room in the mansion that should be shown on the blueprint.
Another detective arrives, and the group gets a call from the house phone in the garage, which sounds like groans of distress.
A circular light shines on the wall, with the shadow of a bat in its center, but after investigating, the group finds that the shape was caused by a miller moth on a car headlight.
The doctor has the niece recreate the nephew's murder, and she notes that she tucked the blueprint in a bread roll on a tray, but the blueprint is now gone.

The new gardener is revealed to be the cashier, and the other detective attempts to arrest him for robbery, murder, and impersonation, but the niece stops him, revealing that she and the cashier are engaged.
The doctor searches for the hidden room by knocking on walls, which causes the others to investigate the sound, leading them to a ballroom which is supposedly haunted.
The candles in the ballroom go out when lit, and a shape appears to float towards the other detective and the maid, but it turns out to be the Japanese butler carrying a lamp.
After being confronted by the detective, the doctor knocks the detective unconscious by striking his head, and he hides the detective's body in another room.
A beaten man enters the house, and the other detective finds that he has no identification on his person.
The butler sees a mysterious figure wearing a hat, and as he leaves to tell the others, the criminal's shadow passes by the door.
The criminal sets up a system of wires that attach to a light switch.
Outside, the cashier sees the figure in the hat crossing the roof, and realizes that it is the supposedly dead bank president.
The niece finds the hidden room, located behind a fireplace.
The criminal confronts her, demanding the combination to the safe in the hidden room, but she escapes.
The doctor is accused of helping the criminal, and the criminal is soon captured and held at gunpoint.
However, the criminal activates the wire system, turning off the lights and allowing himself to escape.
The criminal flees outside but his leg is caught in the bear trap placed earlier by the maid.
The others find him and remove his mask, revealing him to be the detective.
The beaten, unknown man announces that he is the true detective, and that the man underneath the criminal's mask had stolen his papers, locked him in the garage, set it on fire and impersonated him.
Following the war, the hero sets himself up as a opium drug kingpin and warlord abroad.
A mysterious holy man who exhibits psychic abilities abducts the hero and offers him a chance to become a force for good.
The hero initially refuses and is attacked by the holy man's mystical flying dagger after the hero tries to steal it.

Ultimately, the hero becomes the holy man's student and develops psychic abilities of his own, including how to hypnotize others and bend their perceptions so that he becomes invisible, save for his shadow.
The hero returns to the city seven years later and resumes his former life as a wealthy playboy, while secretly operating as a vigilante who terrorizes the city's underworld.
He recruits some of those he saves from criminals to act as his agents, providing him with information and specialist knowledge.
His identity is largely unknown, especially to his uncle, who happens to be the city's police commissioner, whom he has to regularly hypnotize in order to keep the police from interfering with him.
The hero's secret identity is endangered upon meeting a socialite who is also telepathic.
A powerful rogue protégé of the holy man arrives in the city inside his ancestor's sarcophagus.
As the ancestor's last descendant, the villain plans to fulfill his ancestor's ambitions of world domination.
He proposes an alliance to the hero, who refuses.

After acquiring a rare coin from the villain, the hero learns that it is made of a metal that could be used for nuclear fission, and that the socialite's father—a scientist working on energy research for the government—has become uncharacteristically reclusive and aloof.
The hero deduces that the villain has compelled the scientist to create an atomic bomb.
The villain hypnotizes the socialite and commands her to kill the vigilante.
The hero breaks the villain's hypnotic hold on her, but she learns his secret identity.
The scientist's assistant allies with the villain to produce a working bomb, which the villain uses to hold the city to ransom.
The vigilante eventually discovers the villain's location: a luxurious hotel, a building that the villain has rendered forgotten and invisible to the city's inhabitants.

Entering the hotel for a showdown with the villain, the vigilante is subdued by the dagger before he turns it against the villain, disrupting the villain's hypnotic control over the scientist and the city.
While the socialite and the scientist disarm the bomb, the vigilante pursues the villain through the hotel and defeats him by telekinetically hurling a broken shard of glass into his frontal lobe.
The villain awakens in the padded cell of a mental hospital.

One of the doctors tells the villain that they were able to save his life by removing a part of his brain, nullifying the villain's psychic abilities, before walking away and revealing a ring the vigilante gives to his agents.
The hero and the socialite begin a relationship and join forces to fight the criminal underworld.
